pages.imagePrompt: Rainbow Bridge after morning rain, slick wooden planks, arched bridge over winding stream. Bobo monkey gripping Grove team banner pole, striped tail high, confident grin. Spring Fair parade gathering.
pages.text:
Rainbow Bridge was slippery after morning rain. Bobo the monkey didn't notice. He had the Grove team banner, the wind, and a very fast plan.

Spring Fair was open now. Friends lined up for the parade walk across the arched bridge. Below, the stream giggled over smooth stones.

pages.imagePrompt: Mimi rabbit and Timo tortoise holding banner edges, Kiki myna bird overhead. Bobo monkey grabbing middle pole shouting I'll lead. Joyful parade prep on bridge approach.
pages.text:
Mimi held one corner of the banner cloth. Timo walked steady. Kiki flew overhead, counting steps.

Bobo grabbed the middle pole. "I'll lead!" he shouted. "Follow me!"

His striped tail swung. His grin was huge. Faster felt like fun.

pages.imagePrompt: Bobo sprinting onto Rainbow Bridge, boards bouncing, water visible through gaps. Friends calling wait from behind. Motion blur on Bobo.
pages.text:
Bobo sprinted onto the bridge.

The wooden boards bounced. Water shimmered through the gaps.

"Wait for us!" Mimi called.

Bobo didn't wait. Leading meant first. First meant fast.

pages.imagePrompt: Bobo slipping on slick board, mud splash from stream bank hitting legs tail and face. Banner pole wobbling. Friends gasping then laughing.
pages.text:
One board — slick as a banana peel.

Bobo's foot slid. WHOOSH — mud from the stream bank splashed up his legs, his tail, his face.

The banner pole wobbled. Friends gasped — then laughed.

pages.imagePrompt: Bobo laughing awkwardly then face falling. Ears drooping. Heavy disappointed expression while friends still smiling in background.
pages.text:
Bobo laughed too. Ha-ha-ha — because everyone was looking, and laughing felt easier than stopping.

Then the laugh stuck in his throat.

His ears drooped. Something heavy sat on his chest.

pages.imagePrompt: Bobo setting banner down, walking away behind willow tree. Kiki landing calling his name. Bobo not turning around.
pages.text:
"I'm fine!" Bobo called, too loud. He set the banner down and walked away behind a willow tree.

Kiki landed. "Bobo?"

He didn't turn around.

pages.imagePrompt: Behind willow tree Bobo pressing muddy paws to eyes, crying secretly. Intimate close-up, stream and fair soft in background.
pages.text:
Behind the willow, Bobo pressed his muddy paws to his eyes.

Hot tears mixed with mud. He thought no one could see.

He whispered, "I wanted to lead. I wanted to be good."

pages.imagePrompt: Mimi Timo Kiki Gulu sitting in mud beside Bobo under willow — equal eye level, not fixing or wiping. Honest Heart moment friends stay.
pages.text:
Footsteps squelched in the mud.

Mimi sat down beside him — not standing above. Timo sat. Kiki sat. Gulu sat too, quiet.

Nobody wiped his face. Nobody said "it's okay." They just stayed.

pages.imagePrompt: Bobo talking with wobbling voice, friends listening in mud. Warm intimate group shot under willow.
pages.text:
"I'm not fine," Bobo said at last. His voice wobbled. "I'm sad. And muddy. And mad at the mud."

Mimi nodded. "Me too, sometimes — sad and mad at the same time."

Timo said, "We can sit while it hurts."

pages.imagePrompt: Friends carrying banner together across bridge slowly — Mimi Timo Bobo in middle. Walking pace, no sprint.
pages.text:
They sat until Bobo's shoulders stopped shaking quite so hard.

Together they carried the banner back to the bridge. Mimi on one side. Timo on the other. Bobo in the middle — slower now.

pages.imagePrompt: Friends crossing Rainbow Bridge at walking pace, stream below, friends on far bank clapping. Banner held steady.
pages.text:
They crossed Rainbow Bridge at a walking pace. No sprint. No splash.

Friends on the far bank clapped anyway — not for speed, but for showing up.

pages.imagePrompt: Afternoon sun drying banner on grass, Bobo washing face at stream. Friends nearby humming. Gentle relief.
pages.text:
That afternoon, the banner dried in the sun.

Bobo washed his face at the stream. He still felt disappointed — but his friends had seen it.

That felt honest too.
